question: What is the main goal of an electrophysiologic study (EPS)?

options.A: To clear blocked plaque from the coronary arteries
options.B: To measure the exact volume of blood pumped per minute
options.C: To record surface electrical signals without touching the heart
options.D: To map the electrical system of the heart from the inside

explanation: Think of an EPS as an electrical wiring check! Special tiny wires (catheters) are put right inside the heart chambers to see how the electrical signals are flowing. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why would a doctor choose an EPS instead of just a regular ECG?

options.A: An EPS can trigger and pinpoint complex arrhythmias from inside the heart
options.B: A regular ECG only works while the patient is asleep
options.C: A regular ECG is completely unsafe for older adults
options.D: An EPS requires no preparation or recovery time for the patient

explanation: A normal ECG is like looking at the house from the outside. An EPS goes inside the rooms to find exactly where the faulty wiring is causing the fast heartbeats! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h1)

question: Which of these clinical situations is a classic reason to order an EPS?
explanation: When a patient keeps fainting and nobody knows why, doctors use an EPS to check if a sudden dangerous heart rhythm is the sneaky culprit. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h2)

question: A patient with a racing heart and frequent fainting is scheduled for an EPS. What is the main goal?

options.A: To permanently cure high blood pressure using catheter pressure sensors
options.B: To locate the exact electrical pathway causing the abnormal heart rhythm
options.C: To check how well the heart valves open and close during exercise
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries with a small balloon

explanation: Spot on! The goal is pure detective work: tracking down the exact electrical short circuit that's making the heart race. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h2)

question: Why are heart-rhythm medications often stopped before an EPS?

options.A: To keep the access site veins from collapsing during catheter insertion
options.B: To allow doctors to successfully provoke the abnormal heart rhythm
options.C: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the procedure
options.D: To lower the patient's baseline blood pressure safely

explanation: It sounds backwards, but doctors actually *want* to see the bad rhythm happen so they can fix it. If the antiarrhythmic drugs are working too well, they might hide the problem during the test! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which of these is a standard pre-procedure nursing duty before an EPS?

options.A: Verifying that informed consent has been properly obtained
options.B: Keeping the patient running on a treadmill for a stress baseline
options.C: Permanently implanting a pacemaker before the test
options.D: Administering a double dose of blood thinners that morning

explanation: As a nurse, making sure the patient understands the procedure and has signed their consent form is a vital safety step every single time. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is a major nursing responsibility while an EPS is actively happening?

options.A: Monitoring continuous heart rhythms and blood pressure
options.B: Performing surgical closure of the blood vessel access site
options.C: Interpreting the final medical billing codes for the procedure
options.D: Personally advancing the catheter electrodes into the heart

explanation: You are the patient's eyes and ears! Keeping a close eye on the monitors and vitals keeps the patient safe while the team works inside the heart. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why must a working defibrillator be kept close by during an EPS?

options.A: Dangerous heart rhythms are purposely triggered during the test
options.B: Sedation medications frequently cause permanent heart stoppage
options.C: The equipment is required to warm up the contrast dye
options.D: All patients suffer sudden cardiac arrest during catheter insertion

explanation: Because the doctors intentionally spark those weird rhythms to study them, the team must always be ready with a defibrillator just in case the heart needs help getting back to normal. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why must a patient keep their affected leg straight and flat after a femoral EPS?

options.A: To prevent bleeding and hematoma formation at the vascular access site
options.B: To allow the newly mapped heart chambers to settle into position
options.C: To ensure the patient stays awake during the recovery phase
options.D: To help the local anesthesia wear off faster in the leg muscles

explanation: Bending that leg right after a catheter goes into the groin artery is a recipe for bleeding. Keeping it straight protects the clot so the puncture can heal safely! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is an essential post-procedure nursing check after an EPS?

options.A: Checking deep tendon reflexes in both upper arms
options.B: Removing all intravenous lines right before transport
options.C: Checking pulses and color in the extremity used for catheter insertion
options.D: Asking the patient to stand up and walk around immediately

explanation: Always check the foot pulses, warmth, and color on the side where the catheter went in. Good circulation checks catch bleeding or blocked blood vessels early! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h5)

question: An EPS report shows dangerous heart rhythms that couldn't be fixed with ablation. What might the medical team look at next?

options.A: Preparing the patient for discussion about an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator
options.B: Removing all cardiac monitoring equipment permanently
options.C: Scheduling an immediate open-heart surgery for valve replacement
options.D: Discharging the patient with no further restrictions or medications

explanation: When an abnormal pathway can't be successfully ablated away, an implantable device (like an ICD) is often the next line of defense to keep the patient safe from sudden cardiac arrest. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is the nurse's main role when reviewing EPS results with a patient?

options.A: Rewriting the physician's surgical report for legal hospital records
options.B: Diagnosing the primary cause of the heart rhythm disorder independently
options.C: Deciding which antiarrhythmic drug brand the pharmacy should dispense
options.D: Translating technical findings into clear discharge and care instructions

explanation: Medical reports can sound like Greek to patients. As a nurse, you help break down those complex findings so they truly understand how to take care of themselves at home. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h6)
